title: Batch native schema metadata checks
changes: Check all native prototype tables in one guarded SQLcl session instead of starting a session for every table.
Bind each metadata row to its exact source block and table, retaining the existing column, key, identity and trigger checks.
Reject missing, duplicated, reordered, cross-bound or unexpected output; keep normal target authority, freshness and no-replay rules.
limitations: Advisory progress is not technical verification or business acceptance. Unavailable progress is not success; failed claims still require reconciliation, not automatic retry.
Server-side preparation must be configured and tested by the operator; a source release does not enable it.
This hosted preparation route accepts one FMB per request; MMB, OLB and PLL require the separate supported preparation route.
The focused prototype profile, current authority endpoint and private browser worker require explicit operator configuration and live checks.
Real-file OPAF-to-APEX import, authenticated runtime and downloadable export acceptance remain pending.
Any changed candidate requires its own independent review; a saved review is reusable only for the exact reconstructed candidate it approved.
Upgrade preservation does not close a failed run or idle audit, or authorize schema preparation, retry, import or acceptance. Those remain separate gates.
A recorded validation continuation that returns to ATTENTION still requires operator reconciliation; refreshing the page does not restart it.
Technical identifiers are retained; redaction receipts are not complete PII certification or processing permission.
APEX generated, technical checks passed and business acceptance remain separate.
A prototype export does not prove clean-schema reimport, customer-target compatibility or business equivalence.
Release notes describe software changes, not proof of a successful conversion.
